text:
emma: opened a small PR to fix streaming+pagination+retry snippets across py/ts/go — they caused confusing behavior for partial pages and leaked contexts. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4178
raj: nice, which language has the worst offender?
sasha: Go snippet leaked ctx and never closed the stream. Python example didn't show how to persist page token before reading items so retries could restart safely. TS had a retry example but no jitter.
emma: I updated Go to show context.WithCancel + defer resp.Close(), switched iteration to resp.Next() so Close gets called on errors.
emma: Python now shows storing next_page_token before processing items and a tiny helper that retries with backoff.
raj: can you paste the old Python pattern vs new?
emma: old: ``python
resp = client.list_items(req)
for item in resp.items: process(item)
# if error mid-loop, no resume token used
``
new: ``python
resp = client.list_items(req)
page_token = resp.next_page_token
for item in resp.items:
  process(item)
# on transient error: retry using saved page_token to resume
``
jordan: unit test idea 1: mock a page that raises half-way then ensure the code retries from saved token. helps CI catch regressions.
sasha: added a comment about backoff: base=100ms, factor=2, max=5s, add full jitter.
emma: I also fixed a dead link in pagination guide and added a short migration note for SDK v1 -> v2 behavior.
docs-bot: PR 4178 linked to DOCS-305, reviewers: @raj @sasha. CI pending.
raj: quick nit 1: clarify session timeout vs per-call timeout in the Python snippet.
emma: addressed the nit and pushed. will squash after CI passes.
sasha: LGTM from infra side once tests are green.
emma: thanks all, merging after green CI. :thumbsup:
